MMS has a few extra requirements beyond just having data. Let's work through these on your phone:

**1. Reset your APN settings (most common remaining cause)**
MMS needs a correct MMSC URL, which lives in your APN settings. If it's blank or incorrect, picture messages will fail even with data working for browsing.
- Go to **Settings → Cellular/Mobile Data → Cellular Data Network** (on some phones: **Settings → Connections → Mobile Networks → Access Point Names**).
- Open the menu (⋮) and choose **Reset to default**.
- Then **reboot your phone** — the change only takes effect after a restart.

**2. Check Wi-Fi Calling**
If Wi-Fi Calling is ON it can sometimes interfere with MMS. Go to **Settings → Cellular/Mobile Data → Wi-Fi Calling** (or **Settings → Phone → Wi-Fi Calling**) and turn it **OFF**.

**3. Check the messaging app's permissions**
The messaging app needs access to your photos/storage and SMS. Go to **Settings → Apps → Messages → Permissions** and make sure **Storage/Photos** and **SMS** are set to **Allow**.

**4. Check Data Saver**
If Data Saver is on it can block background data for messaging. Go to **Settings → Cellular/Mobile Data → Data Saver** (or **Connections → Data Usage → Data Saver**) and turn it **OFF**.

Once you've done those — especially the APN reset plus reboot — please try sending another picture message. Let me know exactly what it says, and if it's still failing after all of that I'll get you over to our technical support team who can dig into your line from their side.
